questions.stem: Police recovered a body from a river. They were asking to know whether the person drowned himself or it was disposed of. The reliable signs of drowning at autopsy are all except

options.label: A
options.text: Fine, white froth at the mouth and nose

options.label: B
options.text: The presence of weed, sand etc firmly grasped in the hand

options.label: C
options.text: The presence of a large amount of blood in the stomach and intestine

options.label: D
options.text: The presence of fine froth in lungs and hair passages.

questions.answerText: The presence of a large amount of blood in the stomach and intestine
questions.solutionHtml:
The presence of a large amount of blood in the stomach and intestine

KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 349 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 285-289

questions.stemHtml: Sub-pleural haemorrhages shown in the Image are seen in
questions.solutionHtml:
Drowning
  • The alveolar walls may rupture due to increased pressure during forced expirations, and produce haemorrhages, which when present subpleural are called "Paltauf's haemorrhages"in a case of drowning.
  • Paltaufs haemorrhages are shining, pale pink or bluish-red, and may be minute or 3 to 5 cm. in diameter.
  • They are usually present in about 50% of cases in the lower lobes of the lungs but may be seen on the anterior surfaces of the lungs, and the interlobar surfaces.
  • Red and grey patches may be seen on the surface, due to Paltaufs haemorrhages and patchy interstitial emphysema respectively.






KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 345 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 287

questions.stem: A case of drowning was brought for autopsy. The samples of the lungs were submitted for histopathology. Emphysema Aquosum will be seen in drowning in
questions.solutionHtml:
Seawater
  • Drowning fluid actually penetrates alveolar walls to enter the tissues and the blood vessels.
  • This has been described as emphysema aquosum.
  • It is present in about 80% of cases and is presumptive evidence of death from seawater



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 350 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 287

questions.stem: At autopsy on an infant, it is important to diagnose whether he has respired and whether there is air in the lungs. The following test compares the weight of the body to the lungs:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ploucquet’s test
  • The blood flow in the lung beds is so increased after breathing that their weight I almost doubled from 1/70 of the body weight before respiration to 1135 after respiration.
  • The increase in weight is not constant and is not a reliable indication of breathing.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 411 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 341, 342

questions.stem: Which type of drowning is associated with hyperkalemia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Freshwater drowning
  • In the case of freshwater drowning, hyperkalemia may directly damage the myocardium, decreasing cardiac output reduced.
  • The serum potassium increases (a powerful myocardial toxin).
  • This increased load causes rapid overburdening of the heart and produces pulmonary oedema.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 341 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 284, 285

questions.stem: In freshwater drowning death occurs within 5 minutes of submersion due to ventricular fibrillation. The following reason is responsible for this:

options.label: A
options.text: Total asphyxia is produced due to freshwater

options.label: C
options.text: Hemoconcentration of blood caused by osmotic pressure effect

options.label: D
options.text: Hemodilution, overloading of the heart and hemolysis leading to the release of potassium

questions.answerText: Hemodilution, overloading of the heart and hemolysis leading to the release of potassium
questions.solutionHtml:
Hemodilution, overloading of the heart and hemolysis leading to the release of potassium
  • In the case of freshwater drowning, cardiac arrhythmias leading to ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation occur, probably due to hypoxia and hemodilution.
  • Hypoxaemia and hyperkalemia may directly damage the myocardium, decreasing cardiac output reduced. The serum potassium increases (a powerful myocardial toxin).
  • This increased load causes rapid overburdening of the heart and produces pulmonary oedema.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 341 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 285

questions.stem: Gettler test is based on study ………. level of blood in heart chambers:
questions.solutionHtml:
Chloride

GETTLER TEST:

  • Normally, the chloride content is almost equal in the right and left chambers of the heart and is about 600mg. per 100 ml.
  • When drowning occurs in freshwater, water tends to pass from the lungs to the blood and the blood gets diluted by as much as 72% in 3 minutes, and the blood in the left side of the heart will show chloride content up to 50% lower than usual.
  • In drowning in seawater, water is absorbed from the pulmonary circulation into the alveolar spaces which may be up to 42% and due to the hemoconcentration, the chloride content in the left side of the heart shows an increase of up to 30 to 40%. A 25% difference in chloride is significant.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 349 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 289

questions.stem: A body was recovered from a river bank. However, the police were not sure whether the death occurred due to drowning. One of the following is a sure sign of death due to drowning:

options.label: D
options.text: same Diatoms detected in the bone marrow and drowning water

questions.answerText: same Diatoms detected in the bone marrow and drowning water
questions.solutionHtml:
same Diatoms detected in the bone marrow and drowning water
  • The finding of diatoms in the drowning fluid and the body tissues is in favour of drowning.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 347 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 289

questions.stem: The best tissue sample for diatom’s test:
questions.solutionHtml:
Bone marrow
  • The drowning fluid and the particles in it, e.g., diatoms and planktons, pass from the ruptured alveolar wall into lymph channels and pulmonary veins and thus enter the left heart.
  • Only a live body with circulation could transport diatoms from the lungs to the brain, bone marrow, liver and other viscera, and skeletal muscle. They are also found in the bile and urine.
  • The bone marrow is highly suitable and reliable.
  • The bone marrow of long bones, such as the femur, tibia and humerus or sternum is examined for diatoms.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 347 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 289

questions.stem: A boy jumped into the pool on a winter morning. He suddenly collapsed and sank to the bottom of the pool. The cause of death in Immersion Syndrome is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Reflex cardiac inhibition
  • Immersion syndrome (hydrocution or submersion inhibition): Death results from cardiac arrest due to vagal inhibition as a result of
    • Cold water stimulates the nerve endings on the surface of the body,
    • Water striking the epigastrium,
    • Cold water entering ear drums, nasal passages, and the pharynx and larynx which cause stimulation of nerve endings of the mucosa.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 342 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 284
